objectives.text: Keep the 1859 boundary against Guatemala's claim, and have it settled by the International Court of Justice rather than by force or by bilateral bargaining. The 2008 pact sent the question to the court; the referendums passed in both countries by May 2019, written arguments closed in June 2023, and oral arguments began in November 2025 (Wikipedia). The ICJ case page redirected and was not read, so the hearing dates are tier 4.

Keep the economy solvent with tourism and the 2021 debt-for-nature swap. Belize bought back its commercial debt with blue bonds of about US$364 million, financed by a Nature Conservancy loan, and committed to marine protection on 30% of its waters by 2026 (search summary of IMF and press coverage; the IMF page was not read).

means.text: Legal track at The Hague: the 2008 special agreement with Guatemala, the court as referee, and no bilateral concession on the boundary. This is the instrument Belize uses instead of military or treaty backing; its diplomatic seats (Commonwealth, OAS, UN, WTO, CELAC) are already in the datasets, with the citations there.

Tourism as the main earner of foreign exchange, with the United States and retired US residents as the core visitors and expatriate remittances as a second channel (Coface, search summary). Tourism is the lever of the economy, and it is exposed to hurricanes.

constraints.text: No army of its own to hold the line. Britain stationed troops in British Honduras against a Guatemalan invasion; since 1999 both states have kept troops on a one-kilometre adjacency zone along the 1859 line (Wikipedia, tier 4 pointer). The British garrison and the ICJ are the two forms of protection, and neither is a treaty guarantee in any source read.
Small, hurricane-exposed economy. Coface lists dependence on tourism and on US visitors and remittances as the main weaknesses, and notes the exposure of farming and tourism to severe weather.

paradoxes.text: The 2008 pact was meant to take the claim off the bilateral table. The referendums took eleven years and the hearings have not closed, so the claim stays open in every bilateral and multilateral meeting while the court deliberates. Waiting for law is also what keeps the dispute alive.

grand_strategy.reading: Belize's strategy is to keep its 1859 boundary by making law the arena: since the 2008 pact the claim has been before the ICJ, and Guatemala has not accepted the treaty that settled the line. Its money is tourism and a debt swap that bought room without ending its dependence on outside creditors and on the British garrison for protection. Briceño's PUP was re-elected on 12 March 2025 with 26 of 31 seats (Jamaica Observer, search summary), so the policy of waiting for the court is set to run through the next term.

stances.note: The rival side of the territorial dispute. Belize's own territory is own_territory on its side and is not written as a self-stance. Rival, not adversary: Belize has sent the claim to the ICJ and reads Guatemala as a legal opponent, not as a state whose existence is in question (Wikipedia index, tier 4). Bond grievance: the open claim is the wound. The mirror of Guatemala's claimed_territory is written in data/stances/GTM.yaml. Confidence C: tier 4 pointer only; no Belizean government statement was read.

The former colonial power and the garrison's host ties: Britain stationed troops in British Honduras to secure the region, and Belize became independent in 1981 (Wikipedia index, tier 4). No treaty guarantee was read, so the grade stays partner, not ally. Bond kin is our reading, as the brief asks: shared language, legal system and colonial history, and the Commonwealth membership already in the dataset (Wikidata rows). Not a source's word for kinship. Trend stable: no source read shows a movement either way. Confidence C: tier 4 index plus the dataset membership row.

Diplomatic recogniser of the Republic of China (Taiwan), full relations, per the recognition dataset row (Wikipedia index, tier 4). No treaty and no alliance, so partner, not ally. Bond none is our reading: no shared identity and no open grievance in any source read. The date of recognition is not in the sources, so since stays null. Confidence C: tier 4 index only.

stances_toward.note: United Kingdom has not written its reading of Belize; the atlas mirrors Belize's 'partner' reading as 'partner' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

Guatemala's claim to the territory of Belize, written by hand from this side as the mirror of the Belize card (data/stances/BLZ.yaml). The 1859 Wyke-Aycinena treaty, which Guatemala negotiated, recognised British sovereignty over the region; Guatemala later renewed the claim, and in 1999 shifted back to inheriting Spanish and Federal Republic of Central America rights (Wikipedia index, tier 4). Grade read from the claim, not from the rhetoric. Bond grievance: an open historical wound, the claim itself. Confidence C: tier 4 pointer only; no Guatemalan government statement was read.
Taiwan has not written its reading of Belize; the atlas mirrors Belize's 'partner' reading as 'partner' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

relations_from.summary: Belize seeks Guatemala's recognition of the 1859 boundary, which Guatemala accepted in the Wyke-Aycinena treaty. Guatemala has not accepted it since 1999, and the question is before the ICJ.

Belize routes the boundary question to the International Court of Justice under the 2008 special agreement with Guatemala. Oral arguments began in November 2025 (Wikipedia, tier 4); the ICJ record was not read.

relations_to.summary: Guatemala claims the territory of Belize. It argues that the 1859 treaty is void because the road it promised was never built, and since 1999 it claims inheritance of Spanish and Federal Republic of Central America rights; both states agreed in 2008 to send the question to the ICJ.
